# ICC day 1 and day 2 (with outliers; loadings method)

Day 1:
- FA is made for day 1
- Loadings are obtained
- Factor scores are obtained

Day 2:
- Factors scores are obtained given the parameters from day 2 and loadings from day 1


# Correlations between the loadings of day 1 and day 2

```{r}
# Function to perform FA and compute factor loadings correlation
# df_1 <- df_1_og
# df_2 <- df_2_og

# Shared participants
common_ids <- intersect(row.names(df_1), row.names(df_2))

# Filter each df to include only shared participants
df1_common_full <- df_1 %>% filter(row.names(df_1) %in% common_ids)
df2_common_full <- df_2 %>% filter(row.names(df_2) %in% common_ids)


# Get loadings for the intersection of participants for both days
df1_common <- df1_common_full %>%
  select(rlwm_alpha, gng_beta, gng_eps, frgng_exit, phys_k) %>%
  # Filter out the na row
  filter(rlwm_alpha != "NA")

df2_common <- df2_common_full %>%
  select(rlwm_alpha, gng_beta, gng_eps, frgng_exit, phys_k) %>%
  # Filter out the na row
  filter(rlwm_alpha != "NA") 


compute_fa_and_correlation <- function(df_1, df_2, num_factors) {
  # Compute FA for the specified number of factors
  fa_res_rotated_day2 <- factanal(x = df_2, factors = num_factors, rotation = "varimax", scores = "regression")
  fa_res_rotated_day1 <- factanal(x = df_1, factors = num_factors, rotation = "varimax", scores = "regression")
  
  # Extract the factor loadings for both days
  loadings_day1 <- fa_res_rotated_day1$loadings
  loadings_day2 <- fa_res_rotated_day2$loadings
  
  # Compute correlation between factor loadings for each factor
  loadings_correlation <- cor(loadings_day1, loadings_day2)
  
  # Return the correlation matrix
  return(loadings_correlation)
}

# Compute and print the correlation for 4 factors
# loadings_correlation_4 <- compute_fa_and_correlation(df_1, df_2, num_factors = 4)
# print("Correlation for 4 factors:")
# print(loadings_correlation_4)
# 
# # # Compute and print the correlation for 3 factors
# loadings_correlation_3 <- compute_fa_and_correlation(df_1, df_2, num_factors = 3)
# print("Correlation for 3 factors:")
# print(loadings_correlation_3)

# Compute and print the correlation for 2 factors
loadings_correlation_2 <- compute_fa_and_correlation(df1_common, df2_common, num_factors = 2)
print("Correlation for 2 factors:")
print(loadings_correlation_2)
```

## Reliability of parameters for day 1 (only those who did retest) and day 2

```{r}
# Perform ICC analysis for each variable and store the results
# Get the common column names between df_1_retest_pp and df_2
variables <- intersect(names(df_1), names(df_2))
# variables <- intersect(names(df_1_og), names(df_2_og))

# Filter out only row names that are row names of df_2_og in df_1_og
# df_1_og_only_2 <- df_1_og[row.names(df_2_og), variables, drop = FALSE]


# List to store ICC results
icc_results <- list()

# Loop through each variable and calculate ICC
for (variable in variables) {
  icc_result <- icc(cbind(df1_common_full[[variable]], df2_common_full[[variable]]), 
                    model = "twoway", type = "agreement", unit = "single")
  
  icc_results[[variable]] <- list(Variable = variable, 
                                  LB = round(icc_result$lbound, 2), 
                                  UB = round(icc_result$ubound, 2),
                                  ICC = round(icc_result$value, 2))
}

# Convert list to dataframe
icc_df <- do.call(rbind, icc_results)
icc_df <- as.data.frame(icc_df, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Fix the Variable column
icc_df$Variable <- rownames(icc_df)  # Use row names as the correct variable names
rownames(icc_df) <- NULL  # Remove row names after extraction

# Convert numeric columns
icc_df$LB <- as.numeric(icc_df$LB)
icc_df$UB <- as.numeric(icc_df$UB)
icc_df$ICC <- as.numeric(icc_df$ICC)

# Create and print the table
nice_icc <- nice_table(icc_df, title = c("Table 6", "ICC of parameters day 1 & 2"))

# Print preview in Word
print(nice_icc, preview = "docx")



```
## Scatter plots of parameters
```{r}
library(reshape2)


# Get the list of common columns
common_columns <- intersect(names(df_2), names(df_1_retest_pp))

# Create a combined data frame
combined_df <- data.frame()

for (col in common_columns) {
  temp_df <- data.frame(
    df_2_value = df_2[[col]],
    df_1_retest_pp_value = df_1_retest_pp[[col]],
    variable = col
  )
  
  # Calculate Spearman correlation coefficient
  corr_coef <- cor(df_2[[col]], df_1_retest_pp[[col]], method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
  temp_df$corr_coef <- round(corr_coef, 2)
  
  combined_df <- rbind(combined_df, temp_df)
}

# Plotting with ggplot2
plot <- ggplot(combined_df, aes(x = df_2_value, y = df_1_retest_pp_value)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", col = "blue") +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Scatter Plots with Spearman Correlation Coefficients") +
  theme_minimal() +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste("r =", corr_coef)), x = Inf, y = Inf, hjust = 1.1, vjust = 2, size = 3, color = "red", check_overlap = TRUE)

print(plot)



```
## Outlier detection

```{r fig.width=15, fig.height=10}
## Day 1 ##
# Calculate z-scores for each column
z_df_1 <- as.data.frame(scale(df_1))
z_df_2 <- as.data.frame(scale(df_2))

# Mahalanobis distance for df_1
md_1 <- mahalanobis(z_df_1, colMeans(z_df_1), cov(z_df_1))

# Mahalanobis distance for df_2
md_2 <- mahalanobis(z_df_2, colMeans(z_df_2), cov(z_df_2))

# Critical chi-square value for 95% confidence
cutoff_1 <- qchisq(0.95, df = ncol(z_df_1))
cutoff_2 <- qchisq(0.95, df = ncol(z_df_2))

# Find outliers
outliers_1 <- which(md_1 > cutoff_1)
outliers_2 <- which(md_2 > cutoff_2)

# View outliers in original data
df_1_outliers <- df_1[outliers_1, ]
df_2_outliers <- df_2[outliers_2, ]

# Optional: Add a column marking outliers
# df_1$outlier <- md_1 > cutoff_1
# df_2$outlier <- md_2 > cutoff_2

########## older code ##########

# Identify outliers based on z-scores
outliers_df_1 <- which(abs(z_df_1) > 3, arr.ind = TRUE)
outliers_df_1 <- outliers_df_1[order(outliers_df_1[,1]),]

# Extract row and column indices of outliers
z_df_1_long <- pivot_longer(z_df_1, cols = everything(), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "z")
#z_df_1_long$participant <- rep(1:nrow(df_1), each = ncol(df_1))
z_df_1_long$participant <- rep(rownames(z_df_1), each = ncol(df_1))


# Create the scatter plot with abline and colored points
ggplot(z_df_1_long, aes(x = parameter, y = z, color = abs(z) > 3)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(intercept = 3, slope = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_abline(intercept = -3, slope = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text(data = z_df_1_long[z_df_1_long$z > 3 | z_df_1_long$z < -3, ], aes(label = participant), vjust = -0.5, hjust = 0.5, position = position_jitter(width = 0.5, height = 0.1), show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "red"), labels = c("Below 3", "Above 3"))

## Day 2 ##
## TODO: make the indices to be the same across day 1 and day 2
### Construct the df_2 without the outliers
outliers_df_2 <- which(abs(z_df_2) > 3, arr.ind = TRUE)
outliers_df_2 <- outliers_df_2[order(outliers_df_2[,1]),]

# Extract row and column indices of outliers
z_df_2_long <- pivot_longer(z_df_2, cols = everything(), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "z")
z_df_2_long$participant <- rep(rownames(z_df_2), each = ncol(df_2))

# Create the scatter plot with abline and colored points
ggplot(z_df_2_long, aes(x = parameter, y = z, color = abs(z) > 3)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(intercept = 3, slope = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_abline(intercept = -3, slope = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text(data = z_df_2_long[z_df_2_long$z > 3 | z_df_2_long$z < -3, ], aes(label = participant), vjust = -0.5, hjust = 0.5, position = position_jitter(width = 0.5, height = 0.1), show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "red"), labels = c("Below 3", "Above 3"))

# Selecting a parameter
```

## Imputing outliers

```{r, echo=FALSE,message=FALSE, results='hide', warning=FALSE}
### Impute the NAs ###

## Day 1
# Create a new dataframe to store the modified values
NAs_out_df_1 <- df_1
outliers_df_1 <- as.data.frame(outliers_df_1)

# Replace the outlier values with NA
for (i in 1:nrow(outliers_df_1)) {
  NAs_out_df_1[outliers_df_1$row[i], outliers_df_1$col[i]] <- NA
}

# Perform multiple imputation using mice
imputed_out_df_1 <- mice(NAs_out_df_1, m = 5, maxit = 50, method = 'pmm', printFlag = FALSE)

# Get the completed data
compl_imputed_out_df_1 <- complete(imputed_out_df_1)

# Preserve original row names
rownames(compl_imputed_out_df_1) <- rownames(df_1)

## Day 2
# Create a new dataframe to store the modified values
NAs_out_df_2 <- df_2
outliers_df_2 <- as.data.frame(outliers_df_2)

# Replace the outlier values with NA
for (i in 1:nrow(outliers_df_2)) {
  NAs_out_df_1[outliers_df_2$row[i], outliers_df_2$col[i]] <- NA
}

# Perform multiple imputation using mice
imputed_out_df_2 <- mice(NAs_out_df_2, m = 5, maxit = 50, method = 'pmm', printFlag = FALSE)

# Get the completed data
compl_imputed_out_df_2 <- complete(imputed_out_df_2)

# Preserve original row names
rownames(compl_imputed_out_df_2) <- rownames(df_2)
```

## 2 factors and 8 params with outliers: outlier detection
```{r,fig.width=15, fig.height=10}
## Day 1 ##
# Calculate z-scores for each column
z_reduced_df_1 <- as.data.frame(scale(reduced_df_1))
z_reduced_df_2 <- as.data.frame(scale(reduced_df_2))

# Identify outliers based on z-scores
outliers_reduced_df_1 <- which(abs(z_reduced_df_1) > 3.29, arr.ind = TRUE)
outliers_reduced_df_1 <- outliers_reduced_df_1[order(outliers_reduced_df_1[,1]),]

# Extract row and column indices of outliers
z_reduced_df_1_long <- pivot_longer(z_reduced_df_1, cols = everything(), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "z")
#z_df_1_long$participant <- rep(1:nrow(df_1), each = ncol(df_1))
z_reduced_df_1_long$participant <- rep(rownames(z_reduced_df_1), each = ncol(reduced_df_1))


# Create the scatter plot with abline and colored points
ggplot(z_reduced_df_1_long, aes(x = parameter, y = z, color = abs(z) > 3.29)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(intercept = 3.29, slope = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_abline(intercept = -3.29, slope = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text(data = z_reduced_df_1_long[z_reduced_df_1_long$z > 3.29 | z_reduced_df_1_long$z < -3.29, ], aes(label = participant), vjust = -0.5, hjust = 0.5, position = position_jitter(width = 0.5, height = 0.1), show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "red"), labels = c("Below 3.29", "Above 3.29"))

## Day 2 ##
## TODO: make the indices to be the same across day 1 and day 2
### Construct the df_2 without the outliers
outliers_reduced_df_2 <- which(abs(z_reduced_df_2) > 3.29, arr.ind = TRUE)
outliers_reduced_df_2 <- outliers_reduced_df_2[order(outliers_reduced_df_2[,1]),]

# Extract row and column indices of outliers
z_reduced_df_2_long <- pivot_longer(z_reduced_df_2, cols = everything(), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "z")
z_reduced_df_2_long$participant <- rep(rownames(z_reduced_df_2), each = ncol(reduced_df_2))

# Create the scatter plot with abline and colored points
ggplot(z_reduced_df_2_long, aes(x = parameter, y = z, color = abs(z) > 3.29)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(intercept = 3.29, slope = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_abline(intercept = -3.29, slope = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text(data = z_reduced_df_2_long[z_reduced_df_2_long$z > 3.29 | z_reduced_df_2_long$z < -3.29, ], aes(label = participant), vjust = -0.5, hjust = 0.5, position = position_jitter(width = 0.5, height = 0.1), show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "red"), labels = c("Below 3.29", "Above 3.29"))
```

## Calculate multivariete outliers


```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}

maha_df_1 <- as.data.frame(mahalanobis(df_1, colMeans(df_1), cov(df_1)))
maha_df_2 <-  mahalanobis(df_2, colMeans(df_2), cov(df_2))

z_maha_df_1 <- scale(maha_df_1)
z_maha_df_2 <- scale(maha_df_2)

# Identify multivariate outliers based on z-scores
out_maha_df_1 <- which(abs(z_maha_df_1) > 3.29, arr.ind = TRUE)
out_maha_df_2 <- which(abs(z_maha_df_2) > 3.29, arr.ind = TRUE)

# Combine the Mahalanobis distances for both days into one data frame
maha_df <- data.frame(Day = c(rep("Day 1", nrow(z_maha_df_1)), rep("Day 2", nrow(z_maha_df_2))),
                      Mahalanobis_Distance = c(z_maha_df_1, z_maha_df_2))

# Plot boxplot
ggplot(maha_df, aes(x = Day, y = Mahalanobis_Distance, fill = Day)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_abline(intercept = 3.29, slope = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_abline(intercept = -3.29, slope = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Mahalanobis Distance Boxplot",
       x = "Day",
       y = "Mahalanobis Distance",
       fill = "Day")
```
